correctness.rationale: The Steele--Beer integral is evaluated exactly with a change of variables. The derivative is the difference between the final integrand and its initial mean. Its derivative has one change of sign at log(q) and its terminal value is negative, proving exactly one optimum for q>1 and strict monotonicity for q<=1. Explicit nonzero signs of both implicit partial derivatives prove strict increase of the optimizing depth. The analytic extension of g/t^2 at (1,0) proves the 3/2 onset; the exponentially small tail gives log(q)+log(log(q)) at high light. Verified against the self-contained standard-library finite tests in verify.py; computations are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original photosynthesis curve is Steele (1962), and the integrated-production expression is close to Bannister (1974) equation (20); the present claim is strictly the complete sharp optimization classification (zero-versus-positive optimum, all-q uniqueness, parameter monotonicity, and both asymptotic laws). Full PDFs of Steele, Bannister and Walsby were materially inspected. The published Idso--Foster (1975) and Murphy (1962) abstracts are relevant but their complete texts were not accessible; those possible implications and general running-mean theorems remain residual priority risks. value.rationale: The question distinguishes ecological photon saturation and photoinhibition, and quantifies when scattering/attenuation can improve instantaneous fixed-biomass production rather than always decreasing useful light. A complete sharp critical boundary, global monotone response and double-log high-light optical-depth scale resolve a naturally dimensionless design choice. The result is nontrivial although conditional on fixed physiology and Beer attenuation; it is not a universal field-management conclusion.
